_readme: How tools/requirements_to_json.py reads the client's requirements workbook. One entry per sheet that holds requirements.
columns: normalized field -> header text (exact, case-insensitive) OR column letter ('D') OR 1-based index (4). Missing fields stay empty.
Normalized fields: id, epic, title, description, acceptance_criteria, exclusions, references, phase, sources, priority, owner. Anything else goes to 'extra' if listed under extra_columns.
If the client list has no ids, set id to null and an id is generated as <id_prefix><row number>.
Output: docs/reference/requirements.json = {source_file, requirements:[{id, group, epic, title, description, acceptance_criteria, exclusions, references[], phase, sources[], extra{}}], legend{}}

sheets.sheet: <<PLACEHOLDER: sheet name holding functional requirements, e.g. 'Functional Requirements'>>

columns.id: <<PLACEHOLDER: header text of the id column, or null to generate ids>>
columns.epic: <<PLACEHOLDER: header of the epic / area / capability column>>
columns.title: <<PLACEHOLDER: header of the title column>>

sheets.sheet: <<PLACEHOLDER: sheet name holding technical / non-functional requirements, or delete this entry>>

phase_values_in_scope: <<PLACEHOLDER: phase token(s) that count as 'first go-live', e.g. MVP; used for the KPI 'MVP requirements with gap'>>
